title: Independent NGC2 responsibility and acceptance file
question: What did the Army independently require, select, validate, operate, retain, and leave unresolved across Anduril, Palantir, Raft, alternate implementation teams, commanders and Soldiers?

public_decision_chain.observation: The Chief of Staff of the Army approved a Capability Characteristics of Need; an Army Futures Command product owner and an acquisition program manager were identified as the public planning pair.
public_decision_chain.current_ceiling: public requirement authorship and competitive strategy
public_decision_chain.missing: complete CoN bytes, versions, redlines, stakeholder contributions, threshold definitions and approval record

public_decision_chain.observation: PEO C3N established a formal NGC2 program office with a named Army program manager.
public_decision_chain.missing: complete delegated-authority, decision, custody and responsibility matrix

public_decision_chain.observation: The Army awarded Team Anduril an eleven-month prototype OTA for an integrated 4th Infantry Division NGC2 stack through a common data layer.
public_decision_chain.missing: proposal denominator, evaluation, statement of work, team schedule, rights, milestones and acceptance criteria

public_decision_chain.observation: The Army awarded a separate prototype effort for the 25th Infantry Division, preserving a second divisional implementation path.
public_decision_chain.missing: complete team identity, evaluation, component differences, matched performance and later substitution outcomes

public_decision_chain.observation: The 4th and 25th Infantry Divisions used NGC2 stacks in increasingly realistic and contested exercises; commanders and Soldiers tailored views and supplied operational feedback.
public_decision_chain.missing: complete event plans, test cards, performance measures, defect lists, rejected technologies, overrides, aborts, near misses and after-action reports

public_decision_chain.observation: The Army announced a broad Right to Integrate effort across multiple prime and technology firms to force cross-platform interoperability.
public_decision_chain.missing: completed interface transfers, equal rights, conformance outcomes and enforcement against incumbents

public_decision_chain.observation: After operational validations and ten months of feedback, the Army established a common data layer baseline: Anduril leads the baseline and 4th Infantry Division full stack; Palantir supplies Foundry within the Lattice-linked edge-to-cloud mesh; Raft supplies registries, transformation and federation; Lockheed leads the 25th Infantry Division full stack.
public_decision_chain.current_ceiling: selected common data baseline and named operating roles
public_decision_chain.missing: decision memorandum, scored alternatives, interface-control documents, contract modifications, source code and data rights, security authorizations, final acceptance and post-delivery performance

public_decision_chain.observation: The Army described PC-C6 as a later culminating division-scale force-on-force validation while moving from prototyping toward delivery.
public_decision_chain.current_ceiling: delivery transition before final culminating evidence
public_decision_chain.missing: PC-C6 results, acceptance decisions, rejected components, fielding authority, sustainment and termination outcomes

propositions.claim: The Army, rather than Palantir or Anduril, held the documented mission, requirement, award and program-management sovereignty for the frozen NGC2 increment.
propositions.support: Official records identify the Army-approved Characteristics of Need, product owner, acquisition program manager, PEO program office, awards and baseline decision.
propositions.counterevidence: Industry teams materially shaped technical implementation and continuous requirements through operational feedback.

propositions.claim: Palantir and Anduril were operationally integrated in a named NGC2 data-baseline and 4th Infantry Division implementation rather than merely co-present in the market.
propositions.support: The Army assigns Anduril the common baseline and 4th Infantry Division lead and identifies Palantir Foundry inside the Lattice-linked data mesh; operational events exercised an integrated stack.
propositions.counterevidence: The complete interface, acceptance and responsibility record is not public; integration is customer-directed and includes Raft and many other firms.

propositions.claim: Raft performed a distinct registry, transformation and federation organ in the selected common data baseline.
propositions.support: The Army's baseline decision explicitly assigns these functions to Raft.
propositions.counterevidence: No complete custody, version-control, rights or replacement record is public.

propositions.claim: The Army finally accepted the complete NGC2 stack for production fielding by June 22, 2026.
propositions.support: The Army selected a common data baseline after operational validations and moved the effort toward delivery.
propositions.counterevidence: A later PC-C6 culminating validation remained planned; full component acceptance, fielding and sustainment decisions are absent.

propositions.claim: Commanders and Soldiers retained meaningful human authority rather than merely appearing in a nominal human-in-the-loop role.
propositions.support: Official operational accounts state that commanders retain final judgment, tailor views and applications, and provide feedback during exercises.
propositions.counterevidence: The exact information presented, latency, confidence, practical rejection authority, override, abort and responsibility logs are not public.

propositions.claim: NGC2 was a single closed Anduril-Palantir implementation with no meaningful alternative.
propositions.support: The Army awarded and operated a separate divisional implementation and later retained different full-stack leads, additional vendors and competitive onboarding.
propositions.counterevidence: Program-level plurality does not establish competition or substitutability inside the selected common data baseline.

propositions.claim: The public record identifies every rejected component, failed path and reason for exclusion in the frozen increment.
propositions.support: Official accounts acknowledge challenges, improvements and technologies that needed work.
propositions.counterevidence: No complete proposal, component, test-card, rejection, defect or termination ledger is public.

propositions.claim: The Army retained complete software, data, interface, evidence, security, migration and termination rights sufficient for practical vendor substitution.
propositions.support: The Army describes competition, replaceable applications, open integration and public program authority.
propositions.counterevidence: The governing OTAs, interface-control documents, data and software rights, authorization packages, transition clauses and completed migrations are unavailable.

propositions.claim: The Army independently preserved a complete end-to-end evidentiary record across sensor inputs, data transformations, model outputs, user actions and mission effects.
propositions.support: The Army operates the program and exercises, while official records identify distinct vendor data and registry roles.
propositions.counterevidence: No authoritative log, retention, access, version, discovery and responsibility matrix is public.

propositions.claim: The NGC2 integration establishes one common private governance compact or system-wide corporate purpose among Anduril, Palantir, Raft and Lockheed Martin.
propositions.support: The official record shows differentiated vendor functions inside an Army-authored mission and acquisition structure.
propositions.counterevidence: Local teaming and recurring integration remain real and require continued rights and coordination review.

decisive_acquisition_contract.falsifier: Independent decision and test records show that the named vendors did not materially share operative responsibilities, the common baseline was not used or accepted, commanders lacked meaningful authority, and alternate components were practically substitutable with complete Army-controlled records and rights.
decisive_acquisition_contract.stopping_rule: Preserve deployment-specific integration and Army mission sovereignty at their current ceilings; do not claim final production acceptance, practical exit, meaningful human veto, common private governance or coercive effect until the exact missing records close those transitions.

current_result.best_current_explanation: Army-authored competitive prototype and delivery program with real multi-vendor operational integration, a selected Anduril-led common data baseline, distinct Palantir and Raft roles, two divisional full-stack leads, stated commander authority, and unresolved final acceptance, rights, custody, veto and failure records
